title: Exporting data to CSV
body: DataBridge supports CSV export from version 3.0 onward. Go to Workspace → Datasets, select a dataset, and choose Export → CSV. Exports over 1 million rows are processed asynchronously and delivered as a download link by email. On versions before 3.0, CSV export is not available in the UI; use the /v2/exports API endpoint instead. Scheduled recurring exports require the Enterprise plan.

title: Configuring Single Sign-On (SSO)
body: SSO via SAML 2.0 is available on Team and Enterprise plans. In Admin → Security → SSO, upload your identity provider metadata XML and map the email attribute. After enabling enforced SSO, password logins are disabled for all members except break-glass admins. Changes take up to 10 minutes to propagate.

title: API rate limits
body: The DataBridge API allows 600 requests per minute per workspace on Team plans and 3000 requests per minute on Enterprise. Exceeding the limit returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header. Batch endpoints (/v2/batch) count as one request per call regardless of payload size. Rate limit increases can be requested through support for Enterprise accounts.

title: Upgrading self-hosted DataBridge from 2.x to 3.x
body: Version 3.x requires PostgreSQL 14 or newer and Redis 7. Before upgrading from 2.x: back up the database, run databridge-cli migrate --dry-run, and review deprecated pipeline syntax (the 'legacy_transform' block was removed in 3.0). The upgrade is not reversible once migrations complete. Typical downtime is under 15 minutes. Customers on 2.9 or older should upgrade to 2.11 first, then to 3.x.

title: Webhook configuration and retries
body: Webhooks are configured under Admin → Integrations → Webhooks. DataBridge signs every delivery with an HMAC-SHA256 signature in the X-DataBridge-Signature header. Failed deliveries are retried with exponential backoff for up to 24 hours (at-least-once delivery — receivers must deduplicate on the event id). Webhook payloads are capped at 1 MB.

title: Backups and data retention
body: Cloud workspaces are backed up continuously with 30-day point-in-time recovery on Enterprise and 7-day on Team plans. Self-hosted deployments are responsible for their own database backups; we recommend nightly pg_dump plus WAL archiving. Deleted datasets are recoverable for 14 days, after which removal is permanent.

title: Troubleshooting pipeline failures after dependency updates
body: Pipeline runs that fail with 'transform module incompatible' usually indicate a connector or runtime dependency mismatch. Check Admin → System → Dependencies for version drift against the compatibility matrix. Self-hosted 3.x requires connector packs 3.x — 2.x connector packs are not forward-compatible. Rolling back a connector pack requires a service restart.
